Here's how democracy actually works: Lobbyists write bills and give them to politicians who can't read. Those politicians vote based on who donated most to their campaign. This chapter is five bills, pre-written, ready to hand to whichever politician you can afford. You're about to become the best lobbyist in history, except your bills actually help people instead of killing them.

Each bill is designed to pass because it gives politicians what they crave: money, votes, and the ability to claim they did something.

## The Treaty Implementation Act: Making It Real

This is your cornerstone legislation. Without it, the treaty is just paper. With it, you redirect {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} annually from death to life.

![Paper treaty goes in, 27.2 billion comes out. From weapons to medicine. You built a money laundering machine for good.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-treaty-implementation-act-making-it-real-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Core Provisions

#### Section 1: Authorization

- "The United States shall implement the [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-percent-treaty-paper-2025] [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] upon ratification by 3+ nations"
- "1% of the United States military budget (currently ~$10 billion) shall be automatically redirected to a [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) Fund as the nation's contribution to the treaty fund."

- "Funds transfer via auditable automated treasury rules on first day of fiscal year"
- No annual appropriation needed (politicians can't kill it later)

##### Section 2: Protection Mechanisms

- **Supersedes Budget Fights:** Treats treaty obligations as mandatory spending. Supersedes annual budget appropriations.
- **Locked In:** Withdrawal from the treaty requires a very difficult 2/3 Senate vote.
- **Protected Funding:** Funds are exempt from sequestration, government shutdowns, and debt ceiling negotiations.
- **Ratchet Clause:** The 1% funding can only increase, never decrease. It automatically scales if other nations increase their commitment. Public referendum can expand it further.
- **Emergency Use Only:** Only a formally declared war can suspend payments. A vaguely defined "conflict" does not qualify.

![Money locked in vault, protected from politicians and shutdown threats. You childproofed the budget.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-2-protection-mechanisms-bw-academic.jpg)

### Avoiding Common Treaty Failure Modes

Treaties fail in predictable ways. They all fail for the same boring reasons. Here's how this one avoids the common killers:

**Reservation Games.** Countries love to sign treaties then add exceptions that gut them. It's like joining a gym but reserving the right to never go. Solution: no reservations permitted. All or nothing. Take it or leave it.

**Ratification Delays.** Sign with fanfare, take a photo, then let it die in committee forever. Your species calls this "diplomacy." Solution: provisional application. Takes effect on signature. Ratification just formalizes what already started.

**Creative Accounting.** Reclassify "military" spending as "peacekeeping" or "homeland security" to dodge obligations. This is beige crime: making theft so procedurally dull that nobody investigates. Reclassifying "military" as "peacekeeping" is the bureaucratic equivalent of stealing someone's car by renaming it "shared mobility infrastructure." Solution: compliance verified by public ledger and independent audits. Relabeling a submarine as "humanitarian infrastructure" will be noticed, because {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} leaves a paper trail that 193 countries, every bondholder with a Bloomberg terminal, and one moderately competent auditor can follow.

**Parliamentary Obstacles.** Executive signs, legislature refuses to implement. Solution: the treaty sets the percentage; Congress implements it through the annual National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), the same way NATO's spending commitments work. After *Medellin v. Texas* (2008), your Supreme Court said not all treaties are self-executing, so this one doesn't try to bypass Congress. It just gives Congress a job to do. The [Incentive Alignment Bond](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) mechanism makes sure they actually do it (by making "forgetting" expensive).

###### Section 3: The Candy for Congress

![Clinical trials fund local jobs, politicians get naming rights. Bribes, but the kind where everyone lives longer.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-3-the-candy-for-congress-bw-academic.jpg)

- Each state gets proportional pragmatic clinical trial funding
- Naming rights for politicians: "The Senator Smith Cancer Center"
- Job creation metrics published quarterly (re-election fuel)
- Local preference for trial sites (pork barrel paradise)

### Why Politicians Will Vote Yes

Your politicians operate in two tribes. One tribe wraps everything in a flag; the other wraps everything in a heart. Same bill, different wrapping paper. The flag tribe hears "cuts waste, supports troops, America leads." The heart tribe hears "healthcare access, reduces inequality, historic expansion." Both tribes hear "your constituents stop dying and start voting for you." The wrapping doesn't matter. The incentive does.

![Politicians get money, voters get results, everyone gets legacy. VICTORY aligned incentives by making corruption productive.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-for-everyone-bw-academic.jpg)

The [Incentive Alignment Bond](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) mechanism funds independent political support for every politician who votes yes. Opposition faces primary challenges. Cured constituents vote. History books write about them positively. All four things politicians actually care about, delivered simultaneously.

### The Legislative Hack

Bundle it with military funding. Politicians rarely vote against military bills (career suicide). Your treaty implementation becomes a tiny rider on a massive bill they have to pass.

![Hide peace treaty inside war bill. War bill always passes. Peace treaty becomes law. You hacked democracy using democracy.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-legislative-hack-bw-academic.jpg)

Once it passes, it's essentially permanent. Repealing it means admitting they're choosing bombs over cures. Political suicide.

## The Authorization Act for your [Decentralized Institutes of Health](../solution/dih.qmd): Creating Your Machine

This creates your [Decentralized Institutes of Health](../solution/dih.qmd) (DIH). The machine that converts bomb money into trial slots.

![The DIH: a machine that converts old healthcare into life extension. You built a factory for not dying.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-authorization-act-for-your-decen-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Structure Designed to Resist Capture

#### Section 1: Establishment

- "A [Decentralized Institutes of Health](../solution/dih.qmd) (DIH) network is created as an independent agency" (not under HHS control)
- "Governed by transparent rules and auditable automation" (not by political appointees)
- "Funded by treaty obligations" (no appropriations needed)
- "Exempt from government hiring rules" (can actually pay competitive salaries)

##### Section 2: Powers

![New agency sits next to FDA, runs global trials, takes private money. FDA finally gets a sibling that doesn't need permission to function.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-2-powers-bw-academic.jpg)

- Can launch and manage any pragmatic clinical trials globally
- Can partner with any organization
- Can operate parallel to FDA (not under it)
- Can accept private funding ([VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025])

###### Section 3: Governance

- No board of directors (can't be captured)
- Collective-choice decisions via [Wishocracy](../solution/wishocracy.qmd) [@wishocracy-paper-2025] voting
- Transparent public-ledger operations (radical transparency)
- Annual public audits (trust through verification)

### The Trojan Horse Approach

Frame it as a "pilot program" or "innovation testbed." Politicians love pilots because they sound temporary and innovative. Don't mention that successful pilots never get cancelled.

![Call permanent program a pilot. Politicians approve pilots. Pilot never ends. You named your Trojan Horse 'pilot program' and they opened the gates.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-trojan-horse-approach-bw-academic.jpg)

Your politicians will approve the pilot because it sounds temporary. Nothing temporary has ever been cancelled on your planet. You have 47 "temporary" government programs from the 1930s still running. The pilot is a permanent program wearing a lab coat.

### The Poison Pills for Opposition

Insert provisions that make opposition toxic:

- Public salary database (shows who's blocking cures)
- Mandatory disclosure of pharma donations
- Real-time voting records on health issues
- Patient testimony requirements (let dying kids speak)

Opposition means explaining why you're against transparency and dying children. Good luck with that.

![Make votes public. Politicians can't vote against curing disease when everyone's watching. Transparency as a weapon.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-poison-pills-for-opposition-bw-academic.jpg)

## The Parallel Track Act: Your Regulatory Revolution

This act creates your [decentralized FDA](../solution/dfda.qmd) [@dfda-spec-paper-2025; @dfda-impact-paper-2025]. It builds a legal pathway for treatments to operate outside the FDA's 17-year death march. Patients get choices. Researchers get freedom. People stop dying while waiting for approval.

![FDA process: slow, centralized, careful. Parallel Track: fast, decentralized, slightly less careful. One saves lives faster, the other saves careers.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-parallel-track-act-your-regulatory-revolution-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Legal Architecture

#### Section 1: The Parallel Pathway

![Patients get drugs faster, AI watches for problems, insurance covers disasters. You built a safety net so you could move faster.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-1-the-parallel-pathway-bw-academic.jpg)

- "Patients may access treatments in active trials with informed consent"
- "Researchers may conduct trials without FDA pre-approval"
- "Insurance must cover parallel track treatments" (critical provision)
- "Results must be publicly reported" (transparency requirement)

**Section 2: Safety Provisions (So They Can't Call You Reckless)**

- AI monitoring for adverse events
- Automatic trial suspension if harm detected
- Mandatory liability insurance for researchers
- Extra protections for vulnerable populations

##### Section 3: The Data Revolution

![Four types of data flow into approval process: trial results, real-world use, patient feedback, foreign trials. FDA discovers other countries also test drugs.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-3-the-data-revolution-bw-academic.jpg)

- All trial data becomes public (after privacy protection)
- Real-world evidence counts toward approval
- Patient-reported outcomes given equal weight
- Foreign trial data accepted (why waste good science?)

### Why Politicians Will Vote Yes (They Have No Choice)

Politicians are terrified of being blamed for the next thalidomide. They are not terrified of being blamed for the 150,000 who die daily from untested treatments. Your species fears the wrong risk by a factor of {{< var type_ii_error_cost_ratio >}}. The pitch is simple: more data makes things safer, not less. Monitoring a million patients in real time catches problems faster than testing a thousand patients for a decade.

![Old way: test on 1,000 people for 10 years, approve drug. New way: monitor 1 million people in real time. You invented crowd-sourced not dying.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-safety-argument-bw-academic.jpg)

Your politicians come in two flavors. One flavor says "freedom" and the other says "access." They mean the same thing but in different fonts. Both flavors vote yes on letting dying people try medicine, because the alternative is explaining on television why bureaucrats should decide who lives.

### The Implementation Trick

Start with terminal diseases only. Nobody argues against letting dying people try treatments. Once it works, expand to chronic diseases. Then everything else. Classic foot-in-door technique.

![The foot-in-the-door strategy. First you let dying people try medicine. Then everyone else gets jealous and wants to try medicine too.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-implementation-trick-bw-academic.jpg)

## The Right to Try Expansion Act: Medical Freedom

Current Right to Try laws are useless. They require FDA permission (defeats the purpose) and manufacturers can refuse (they often do). Here's the version that actually works.

The proof this passes: Montana already did most of it. One state senator got eligibility restrictions deleted in 2023 (Senate 38-12, House 81-19) and licensed for-profit experimental treatment centers in 2025 [@montana-sb535-2025]. Its rules even make each clinic track every outcome and publish a yearly summary. The one missing piece is pooling: fifty clinics' separate annual summaries cannot be added together, so nobody learns at scale. [The 50-state analysis](../appendix/state-right-to-trial-impact.qmd) includes a three-clause data amendment (enroll, pool, publish) that completes the architecture, with impact numbers, a line-item budget, and an adoption playbook. Hand your legislator the amendment with the analysis attached.

![Current process: fill out forms until you die. Proposed process: try the medicine.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-right-to-try-expansion-act-medical-freedom-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Provisions That Matter

#### Section 1: Absolute Right

- "Any patient may access any treatment in trials"
- "Manufacturers must provide at cost + 15%" (reasonable profit)
- "Insurance must cover if cheaper than standard care"
- "No FDA approval needed for dying patients"

![The four pillars of letting people try not to die. It's like the Bill of Rights, but for medicine instead of guns.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-1-absolute-right-bw-academic.jpg)

##### Section 2: The Subsidy System

![Poor people get free medicine. Rich people can afford medicine. The middle gets to choose between medicine and food, like usual.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-2-the-subsidy-system-bw-academic.jpg)

- Subsidies from a [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) Fund make treatments affordable
- Sliding scale based on income
- Full coverage for those below 200% poverty line
- Catastrophic protection for everyone else

###### Section 3: The Data Exchange

![People take medicine. Medicine works or doesn't. We write it down. Medicine gets better. You invented learning, but medical.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-3-the-data-exchange-bw-academic.jpg)

- Patients provide outcome data in exchange for access
- Data improves treatments for everyone
- Creates massive real-world evidence database
- Accelerates learning by 100X

### The Emotional Blackmail Strategy

Politicians already parade dying children at press conferences. You are just changing the script. The new line is one question: "Why won't you let me try to live?"

![Step 1: Dying people tell their stories. Step 2: Politicians feel bad. Step 3: Politicians do something because everyone is watching.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-emotional-blackmail-strategy-bw-academic.jpg)

Create a "Death Clock" website. Show people dying while waiting for treatments available elsewhere. Update it live during hearings. Make opposition morally impossible.

Your species has libertarians, progressives, religious groups, and patient groups. They agree on almost nothing. They all agree dying is bad. When the Koch Brothers and Bernie Sanders agree, politicians panic and pass your bill. This is the only bipartisan coalition in human history that required zero compromise, because "not dying" is not a partisan position. It just looks like one because nobody proposed it.

![The only thing that unites libertarians, progressives, and religious people: everyone agrees dying is bad.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-coalition-building-bw-academic.jpg)

## The Budget Reallocation Act: Moving the Money

This is the technical bill that actually moves the money. Boring but critical. Without it, everything else is theater.

### The Money Flow Mechanics

#### Section 1: Automatic Transfer

- 1% of DoD budget transferred on October 1st annually
- Via Federal Reserve direct transfer into the treaty fund's designated treasury rails
- To a [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) Fund account structure governed by transparent, hard-to-rewrite rules
- Cannot be rescinded or redirected without treaty withdrawal

##### Section 2: The Protection Clauses

- Funds exempt from sequestration
- Exempt from government shutdown
- Exempt from debt ceiling fights
- Treated as treaty obligation, not appropriation

###### Section 3: The Growth Mechanism

![The ratchet only turns one way. Like a socket wrench, but for not dying. Once funding goes up, it stays up.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-section-3-the-growth-mechanism-bw-academic.jpg)

- Automatic increase if other nations increase
- Percentage can only go up, never down
- Success metrics trigger expansion discussions
- Public referendum can force increases

![Treaties beat regular laws. It's in the Constitution. The Founders planned ahead for when future politicians would be idiots.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-constitutional-approach-bw-academic.jpg)

- Treaty obligations supersede regular law
- Supremacy clause makes it difficult to change
- International law prevents backtracking

- Touching it means you're "against the troops" (their healthcare)
- And "against children" (pediatric trials)

#### The Technical Protection

### The Incremental Implementation

![Year 1: Start. Year 5: Everyone realizes this was obvious the whole time.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-incremental-implementation-bw-academic.jpg)

Year 1: Move the money. Fund {{< var dih_patients_fundable_annually >}} trial slots. Publish results.

## The Legislative Strategy: Order of Operations

Here's how you pass all five bills:

### Phase 1: Build Momentum

1. **Right to Try Expansion** goes first (emotional, bipartisan)
2. Creates patient demand for more access
3. Shows system can handle parallel tracks
4. Politicians get credit for "saving lives"

![Sick people get medicine. Medicine works. Politicians notice people like not dying. System reinforces itself like a functional feedback loop.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-phase-1-build-momentum-bw-academic.jpg)

### Phase 2: Create Infrastructure

![Researchers can finally do research. You had to write a law for this.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-phase-2-create-infrastructure-bw-academic.jpg)

1. **The Parallel Track Act** comes next
2. Builds on Right to Try success
3. Creates legal framework for trials
4. Researchers start preparing for new system

### Phase 3: Fund the System

![Three laws walk into a bar. They combine into one mega-law because voting once is easier than voting three times.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-phase-3-fund-the-system-bw-academic.jpg)

1. **The authorization act for your [Decentralized Institutes of Health](../solution/dih.qmd)** establishes the organization
2. **The Treaty Implementation Act** provides the framework
3. **The Budget Reallocation Act** moves the money
4. All three pass together in omnibus package

### The Omnibus Strategy

Package everything in a must-pass bill:

- Military authorization (they always pass)
- Or continuing resolution (government shutdown threat)
- Or debt ceiling increase (economic catastrophe threat)

Politicians can't vote against it without catastrophic consequences. Success becomes highly likely.

![You hide the good stuff inside the bill that funds the government. Like sneaking vegetables into a child's dessert, but for democracy.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-the-omnibus-strategy-bw-academic.jpg)

## Conclusion: Democracy Theater at Its Finest

None of this changes how democracy works. That's the point. Five bills that convert a system profiting from death into one profiting from life.

![Cures create grateful voters. Grateful voters demand more cures. Politicians who resist get voted out. Darwin, but for policy.](/assets/images/legislation-package/legislation-package-section-conclusion-democracy-theater-at-its-finest-bw-academic.jpg)

Once passed, they are nearly impossible to repeal. Every person treated becomes a voter for expansion. Every cure makes the next bill easier to pass. The ratchet only turns one direction.

Politicians do not read bills. Lobbyists write them. This is the lobbyist's playbook, except the client is everyone and the product is not dying.
